label: y/p (u/k/g) right after o, early in a prefix starting with y/l/a/o
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.0035% of steps). It fires mostly in the original phase (83% of mass), peaking at t=2-3, when the input is y (49% of mass) or p (23%), less often u/k/g, and the previous input is o (68% of mass). It is strongly favored when the prefix is made of y/l/a/o letters, e.g. first token y/l/a/o, prev2 o/l. Top examples: y o o [y], a l l o [y], y l x o o [p]. A smaller copy-phase component (17% of mass) fires when y is fed back at recall_idx 1-2 and the sequence starts with y/3. It never fires at t<2 or on the delimiter. The predicate gets about half the activation mass, but precision is only ~0.1: most o->y/p transitions in such prefixes do not activate it, so the real condition likely depends on finer hidden-state context. Magnitude is flat (median 0.11, max 0.21) and no modulating variable was found.
